edges.claim: Binance said 90% of aggregate stolen asset value had been replenished; XRP was among ten assets named for minimum 1:1 verification in the 00:00 GMT October 31 PoR snapshot. No XRP-specific purchase quantity was disclosed.
Reuters reports Binance said it partially deployed its SAFU bitcoin reserve in the aggregate replenishment.
Liqwall reported OI, funding, liquidations and account ratios at 2026-10-31 16:32 UTC; these remain provider-specific and unverified by independent contract-level data.
Binance's page displayed XRP at approximately $1.25 and $1.3B 24-hour volume as of 16:19 UTC.

hypotheses.statement: The reported 90% aggregate replenishment and inclusion of XRP in the named 1:1 coverage set may reduce exchange-counterparty concern once the full proof is independently verifiable.
support: Reuters reports Binance's 90% aggregate claim and the 10-asset 1:1 verification statement.
disconfirming: The full proof was not available at the capture cutoff.
No XRP-specific replacement quantity or reserve-address reconciliation was disclosed.
A company reserve claim is not independent proof of liabilities and assets.
tests_needed: Retrieve the complete post-incident PoR and asset-level XRP liabilities/reserves.
Reconcile proof addresses with pre-incident reserve addresses and the five incident source wallets.
Verify withdrawal restoration and subsequent XRP deposits/withdrawals.

hypotheses.statement: Positive funding, rising open interest and a 73% Binance long-account share may leave leveraged positioning vulnerable to a downside liquidation cascade if spot weakens.
disconfirming: The funding rate is modest; OI rose only 0.9% over 24h; rolling liquidations were $808K at capture.
Account counts are not notional exposure and no contract-level margin distribution is available.
A single provider snapshot cannot establish crowded notional positioning.
tests_needed: Reconcile contract-level OI and funding across Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid.
Obtain notional long/short exposure and liquidation-price distributions.
Compare with realized volatility, spot order-book depth and BTC/ETH controls.

hypotheses.statement: The earlier Binance XRP reserve decline may partly reflect the October 29 theft rather than voluntary customer withdrawals.
support: The incident transfer quantity and some provider reserve changes are similar in magnitude.
disconfirming: Provider wallet universes and timestamps differ; no five-wallet address crosswalk is complete.
Customer withdrawals, wallet migrations and internal reclassification remain alternatives.
tests_needed: Crosswalk all five source wallets against Binance's official reserve-address export and provider labels.
Reconcile customer liabilities and reserve balances at identical timestamps.

policy: Do not convert aggregate reserve coverage into XRP purchases; do not convert account percentages into notional exposure; preserve alternative explanations and source independence.
